explanation.headline: Prochlorperazine is not on FDA's shortage list; three hospital sites hold 17.9 to 18.8 days on hand

sentences.text: FDA's drug shortage list does not include prochlorperazine as of 2026-10-21.
Corvale East holds 139 eachs of the 25 mg suppository at 7.8 a day for 17.9 days on hand.
Corvale General holds 161 eachs at 8.6 a day for 18.8 days on hand.
Corvale Lakeside holds 26 eachs at 1.5 a day for 17.9 days on hand.
The ranked alternate manufacturer is Cosette Pharmaceuticals, Inc., which is not on FDA's shortage list today and its label names no plant we could place.
A second alternate manufacturer is Padagis US LLC, also not on FDA's shortage list today with no plant we could place on its label.
The current label for the product identifies PD-Rx Pharmaceuticals, Inc. as the registered plant with a VAI inspection on 2026-08-20.

memory.text: Decision on carboplatin: restrict carboplatin to curative-intent regimens while on allocation; oncology reviews each palliative order. Rationale: Two suppliers on allocation and under 10 days on hand at Corvale General (demo history). Approved by Jordan Hale, PharmD.

Decision on lidocaine: switch lidocaine 1% 30 mL vials to 5 mL vials in the ED to reduce waste during the shortage. Rationale: Single-dose waste was a third of use (demo history). Approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD.

Decision on cisplatin: transfer cisplatin between Corvale hospitals weekly instead of buying grey-market stock. Rationale: Grey-market offers were 6 to 10 times contract price with unverifiable pedigree (demo history). Approved by Jordan Hale, PharmD.
